structured_output.hypothesis: In 3D-segmented plant cell-wall networks, the dihedral angles between the three cell walls meeting at three-way edges (viewed in cross-section perpendicular to the edge) cluster near 120° independent of the sizes of the adjacent cells.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Across at least 500 three-wall junction edges (more than 10 ovules), the median junction angle is within 120° ± 5°, at least 60% of all individual angles fall within 120° ± 15°, and the absolute Spearman correlation between junction angle deviation and the log ratio of adjacent cell volumes is below 0.2.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The median junction angle lies outside 120° ± 5°, OR fewer than 60% of angles fall within 120° ± 15°, OR the absolute Spearman correlation between angle deviation from 120° and log cell volume ratio is 0.2 or higher (n ≥ 500 junctions).
structured_output.interpretation: 'Cell-walls meeting by threes' means triple-wall edges seen as triple points in a 2D section; 'angle of 120°' means the angle between wall tangents at the junction, measured on a cross-section perpendicular to the edge in 3D segmentations; 'size of the cell' means cell volume (or section area); 'curvature' of walls is a separate secondary quantity. Reinterpretation: the dataset is Arabidopsis ovule primordia (meristematic, small-celled, not mature parenchyma), so this tests the claim in living plant tissue. Plateau's laws are the modern justification; real plant walls are under tension and turgor, so deviations are expected where cell pressures differ. The authors' images are propidium-iodide cell wall stains with ImarisCell segmentation, and the .ims files must be read to extract labeled surfaces.
